items.title: Google Discover Core Update Data: Local Publishers Lost Reach
items.summary: Google's Discover core update, which ran from late January to early March 2026, prioritized locally relevant content, leading local publishers like Syracuse.com to lose significant national reach while holding onto home-state audiences. Major publishers such as Yahoo, Fox, and Forbes experienced sharp declines in out-of-state placements and audience scores. This shift highlights the need for SEO strategies focused on local relevance and tools like DiscoverSnoop for tracking Discover performance.

items.title: SEO vs AEO vs GEO: The Evolution of Search Optimization
items.summary: SEO expert Josh Nay explains how traditional SEO focuses on keywords and backlinks for search results lists, while AEO targets direct answers for AI chatbots and voice search. GEO, the latest trend, optimizes for visibility in AI-generated summaries like Google AI Overviews by emphasizing authority, uniqueness, and structured data. Brands should implement all three strategies in parallel to stay competitive.

items.title: AI Mode Data, Ask Maps & Branded Queries Go Live – SEO Pulse
items.summary: Google's AI Mode has boosted self-citations to 21%, shifting links from external sites to its own results and impacting SEO citations. New Ask Maps feature uses Gemini for conversational queries on Google Maps, stressing the importance of reviews for local SEO. Search Console's branded queries filter now uses AI for better traffic analysis, alongside advances in audio/video indexing.

items.title: GEO + AEO + Agentic SEO: Winning Strategy for AI Answers
items.summary: With 47% of Google searches now featuring AI answers first, focusing on GEO, AEO, and Agentic SEO is crucial for getting cited. The post shares a full 90-day strategy guide to dominate AI search results like Google AI Overviews. Key hashtags highlight the shift in digital marketing toward AI-optimized search.

items.title: 5 Things I Learned About The Future Of Search From Liz Reid’s Latest Interview
items.summary: Google's Liz Reid predicts AI agents will handle web interactions, leading to agent negotiations and web structure changes, while human input remains for personalization. Gemini and Search may converge into new products as AI answers replace traditional search. Google supports high-quality AI-generated content and explores micropayments for paywalled access.

items.title: aeo.js: Open-Source Library for AI Search Engine Visibility
items.summary: Developer Ruben launches aeo.js, an open-source library to make websites visible to AI search engines, along with a free scanner at check.aeojs.org to assess site readiness. This tool addresses the growing need for AEO in the evolving AI search landscape.

items.title: Journalist Sues Grammarly Over Unauthorized AI Editing Feature
items.summary: A journalist filed a lawsuit against Grammarly after the company released an AI feature that edited user text without clear consent, generating suggestions purportedly from real authors including deceased ones. The feature sparked multi-million-dollar legal action from writers whose names were used. This highlights growing AI controversies in writing and editing tools.

items.title: Self-Publishing Scams Supercharged by AI Fraudsters
items.summary: The Guardian reports on Jon's heartbreaking experience with AI-powered book scams targeting self-publishers. Fraudsters exploit the boom in self-publishing using AI to create fake services and swindle authors. This interactive feature underscores risks in the publishing landscape.

items.title: Sarah J. Maas Announces Next Two ACOTAR Books, Sending BookTok into Meltdown
items.summary: Fantasy author Sarah J. Maas revealed the next two books in her A Court of Thorns and Roses series on the Call Me Daddy podcast. The announcement has sparked frenzy among BookTok fans. This major release news boosts excitement in the romance fantasy community.

items.title: Author Betrays Trust by Feeding Manuscript to ChatGPT for Edits
items.summary: Writer Autumn Bauman shares outrage after an editor used ChatGPT to generate an entire edit letter from her manuscript without permission. She also lost design work to Claude AI. The post vents frustration with AI infiltration in publishing and editing processes.

items.title: Grammarly's AI Uses Virtual Versions of Dead Authors Without Permission
items.summary: WIRED's Miles Klee exposes Grammarly's new AI features mimicking real authors, including deceased ones like a historian who died recently, without seeking permission. The tool evolved from proofreading to offering 'expert' feedback via AI agents. This raises ethical issues in AI-assisted writing.

items.title: Goodreads Reveals Cover for V.E. Schwab's 'Victorious', Final Villains Book
items.summary: Goodreads shares the exclusive cover for 'Victorious' by V.E. Schwab, the conclusion to the bestselling Villains series from Tor Books, out October 2026. The three-time Goodreads Choice Award winner's new release generates buzz. Fans encouraged to add it to their shelves.

items.title: Quentin Tarantino Fires Back at Rosanna Arquette Over Pulp Fiction Criticism
items.summary: Rosanna Arquette criticized Quentin Tarantino's use of the N-word in Pulp Fiction as 'racist and creepy.' Tarantino responded in a letter, questioning her change of heart after accepting the role and payment, and accusing her of lacking class for seeking publicity. The Variety post sharing his response garnered significant engagement.

items.title: Viral X Post Shares List of 'Woke' Red Flags in TV and Movies
items.summary: User @SirBylHolte posted a detailed list of common tropes signaling ideological content in entertainment, such as diverse casting in historical settings or female-led narratives overriding male stories, advising viewers to stop watching upon encountering them. The post received over 12,000 likes and resonated with audiences expressing frustration over preaching in media. It highlights viewer strategies to avoid certain content types.

items.title: 'The Bride' Labeled Feminist Monster Film in Box Office Bomb Report
items.summary: ZeroHedge posted about 'The Bride' as 2026's biggest box office bomb, describing it as a feminist monster film amid its financial failure. The update drew attention to ongoing discussions of content impacting audience turnout. It connects to broader conversations on entertainment flops.

items.title: Bill Maher Criticizes Oscars Diversity Complaints and 'Woke' Hollywood
items.summary: Bill Maher on 'Real Time' dismissed ongoing #OscarsSoWhite grievances, citing diverse winners and films, and described Hollywood as a 'secret cabal terrified of looking like racists' enforcing inclusion standards. He claimed 'woke' Hollywood denies him awards for speaking freely. Maher advised progressives to celebrate achievements.

items.title: Pixar’s ‘Hoppers’ Tops Box Office, Ending Original Film Streak
items.summary: ‘Hoppers’ debuted with $46 million domestically and $88 million globally, earning an A CinemaScore and praise as a crowd-pleasing animated hit about talking animals. It represents Pixar's strongest opening for an original in nearly a decade, on track for $500 million worldwide. The performance outshone underperformers like ‘The Bride!’

items.title: ‘The Bride!’ Emerges as 2026’s Costliest Box Office Disappointment
items.summary: ‘The Bride!’ opened to $7.3 million domestically against an $80 million budget and substantial marketing, projecting major losses with a C+ CinemaScore and 58% Rotten Tomatoes score. Audiences struggled to categorize the R-rated Gothic horror-romance. Streaming competition from Oscar-nominated films factored into its weak debut.

items.title: Mastercard Launches Virtual C-Suite Agentic AI for Small Businesses
items.summary: Mastercard is advancing its agentic AI strategy with the Virtual C-Suite, starting with a Virtual CFO tool that brings executive-level intelligence to small businesses. This platform helps SMBs with financial analysis, forecasting, and strategic decision-making previously accessible only to larger enterprises. It aims to level the playing field by automating complex tasks and providing actionable insights.

items.title: LinkedIn Introduces All-In-One AI Tool for Small Business Sales, Marketing, and Hiring
items.summary: LinkedIn has developed an integrated AI-powered tool in its Premium offering specifically for small businesses to streamline sales, marketing, and hiring processes. The tool automates lead generation, content creation, and candidate matching, saving time and boosting efficiency for growing SMBs. LinkedIn's VP of Small Business Marketing highlights its role in helping owners manage multiple functions without specialized teams.

items.title: Why Small Businesses Are the Biggest Untapped AI Automation Opportunity
items.summary: An automation expert recounts securing $200k from a PE firm after automating appointment reminders for their hairdresser business, revealing SMBs as a massive overlooked market for AI. The post breaks down why small businesses are ripe for simple AI wins and shares a playbook for agencies to land high-value clients. It shifts perspective on targeting everyday operations over flashy enterprise deals.

items.title: Real-World AI Tools Built by Small Business Owners Saving Thousands
items.summary: Small business owners are deploying custom AI solutions without coding expertise: a dentist's AI receptionist saves $4k/month, a food truck's predictor cuts waste 40%, a photographer's editor doubles bookings, a gym's churn tool boosts retention 22%, and a pest control CRM replaces expensive software. These examples illustrate AI's practical impact on operations, costs, and growth. The gap between builders and observers widens survival odds.
